description: R08 DeserializationTests action/command seam: safe Rust owns combined actions+keybindings layering, nested-command validation/unbind/rebind, and inherited action/keybinding identity across settings layers.

entries.notes: One portable aggregate reproduces Microsoft's combined action/keybinding layer: five effective keybindings, only the explicitly named ctrl+c command in NameMap, and vertical/horizontal split projection.
Unnamed nested-command parents and their children are ignored without warnings because nested commands cannot receive an autogenerated name.
Named nested commands whose children omit command payloads are rejected with FailedToParseSubCommands plus the CascadiaSettings aggregate warning.
A later commands:null layer removes a previously materialized named nested command.
A later command:newTab definition reuses the parent's named identity and replaces nested children with a concrete action.
A child layer can unbind a key chord inherited from a parent while retaining a separately named ID-backed action with no keybinding.
Child layers replace an inherited action payload by ID, retarget an inherited key chord, and bind a new chord to an action ID that exists only in the parent layer.
